set.approach: Paint Mountain (Tsi Dhal) is on the Whitehorse side of Haines Junction: shortly before the town, just beyond the Pine Lake Campground, turn onto Pine Lake Road and follow it to its end at the small cul-de-sac with trailers, where you park without blocking driveways. From the parking area walk west past a rundown trailer and around a gate, pass a cabin on the left, and follow the trail, which fades in places, while keeping the recessed canyon in view. At a small break in the forest with young aspen you are below the canyon. Go straight uphill through trees and then rock, scramble to the foot of the canyon, and use the fixed rope on the left side to climb the steep gully. The Lower Chunder crags lie on the hiker's right of that approach. Sound Travels is the left-most route developed there; look for white webbing that marks the three-fifths point of the climb.
set.descent_text: Rappel from the rings at the top.

review.notes: Approach from Paint Mountain, Chunder Canyon and Lower Chunder pages and route Location; rap rings noted on the route page.

set.approach: Mount White, south of Whitehorse on the Alaska Highway, is reached by the Conversation approach: from the Jake's Corner junction continue south on the Alaska Highway until the road bends left on a high bank, and look down for a culvert and a telephone pole with flagging tape on its guy wire. Head south toward the range on a faint flagged trail with cut logs and a log bridge to a wash, cross it, and keep to the climber's right of the stream bank up to the waterfall. Aim left from the waterfall over old moraine features and up grassy scree to the base of the big slab. The climbing starts from a flat ledge behind a small spruce.

review.notes: Approach from Conversation and Northwest Buttress pages and route Location. No descent stated (route ends at the rim).

set.approach: The Faces is a steep, roofed granite prow above Bennett Lake near Carcross. Park at the lower mountain-bike lot on Montana Mountain Road, walk or bike the road a short way and take the Fox trail, then turn right downhill past a few berms toward the railway track and follow Wayne's World to where you leave the bikes. No trailhead marker or established path exists from there: head straight up the hill south to an old moraine from which the cliff is clearly visible, then bushwhack uphill as the angle steepens, keeping the cliff in view. Contour below the mossy slabs to a steep gully that leads directly to the base of The Surprise. Carry navigation. Faut Depart starts at the rappel rings on a sloping, grassy ledge and finishes at the large ledge with a bolt anchor.
set.descent_text: A bolted rappel line runs down from the top of the Pry Me climbs.

review.notes: Approach from the cliff page and route text; rap line from the cliff page.

set.approach: The White Range towers are seen from the Klondike Highway across Poole Canyon, found by looking up the valley between Escarpment Mountain and the old burn. They are guarded by Windy Arm, which is crossed by boat or paddle (on skis or foot in winter) to the mouth of Ramshorn Creek. From the alluvial fan, find a way through the trees, burn and meadows to the towers; no trail exists. It sits at the foot of the biggest tower and heads toward the splitter cracks that show from the highway, with a bolt marking the start.
set.descent_text: A bolted rappel station sits to the right of the belay ledge at the top of the first pitch.

review.notes: Approach from the area page and route Location; the rappel station is from the route text (route is unfinished).
